{{short description|Israeli biophysicist}}
'''Naama Barkai''' ({{Langx|he|נעמה ברקאי}}) is an Israeli [[systems biology|systems biologist]] and [[professor]] for [[Molecular genetics|Molecular Genetics]] and [[Physics of Complex Systems]] at the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]] in [[Rehovot]], [[Israel]], and a member of the [[European Molecular Biology Organization]] (EMBO).

== Education and career ==

In 1995, Barkai earned a PhD ''summa cum laude'' in [[theoretical physics]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], on the statistical mechanisms of learning.<ref name="embo_press_release">{{cite web |title=Systems biologist finds novel solutions to fundamental biological problems |url=http://www.embo.org/news/press-releases/2008/systems-biologist-finds-novel-solutions-to-fundamental-biological-problems |accessdate=12 July 2019}}</ref><ref name="bloomberg">{{cite web |title=Bloomberg Executive Profile |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=207074699&privcapId=3274115 |website=Bloomberg Executive Profile |accessdate=12 July 2019}}</ref> Barkai pursued a post-doc in the group of [[Stanislas Leibler]] at [[Princeton University]], where she worked on theoretical analysis of biochemical networks.<ref name="embo_press_release"/> During this time, she was supported by the [[Robert H. Dicke Fellowship]].<ref name="embo_press_release"/><ref name="bloomberg"/> From 2001 to 2004, Barkai was an EMBO young investigator.<ref name="embo_press_release"/> Her work on deciphering mechanisms of control in complex biological systems combining experimental work with mathematical modelling shaped the field of [[systems biology]].<ref name="embo_press_release"/> From 2005 to 2006 she was a visiting professor at [[Harvard University]].<ref name="embo_press_release"/> In 2007, she was elected as EMBO member.<ref name="embo_press_release"/>

She is on the scientific advisory board of [[Evogene Ltd.]]<ref name="bloomberg"/>

== Awards and honours ==

* Rothschild Prize (2018)<ref name="roth">{{cite web |url=https://www.yadhanadiv.org.il/rothschild-prizes |website=Rothschild Prizes|title=Rothschild Prizes recipients |accessdate=12 July 2019}}</ref>
* [[FEBS/EMBO Women in Science Award]] (2008)<ref name="embo_press_release"/>
* Helen and Martin Kimmel Award for Innovative Investigation (2007)<ref name="embo_press_release"/>
* Teva Prize for Research in Systems Biology (2005)<ref name="embo_press_release"/>
* Morris L. Levinson Biology Prize from the Weizmann Institute of Science (2004)<ref name="embo_press_release"/>
* Michael Bruno Memorial Award (2004)<ref name="embo_press_release"/>
